questions.q: Who gathered with David at the cave of Adullam?
questions.a: Everyone who was in distress, in debt, or who did not like what was happening in Israel with Saul as king.

questions.q: How long did David’s father and mother stay with the king of Moab?
questions.a: They stayed with the king the whole time that David was in the stronghold.

questions.q: Who did Saul hear had been discovered?
questions.a: He heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered.

questions.q: What did Saul accuse his servants of not revealing to him?
questions.a: Saul said that none of his servants had revealed to him that his own son had made a covenant with David or had incited David against him.

questions.q: What two things did Doeg the Edomite tell Saul that Ahimelech gave to David?
questions.a: Doeg the Edomite told Saul that Ahimelech gave David provisions and the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

questions.q: What did Saul say Ahimelech did for the son of Jesse besides giving him bread and a sword?
questions.a: Saul said that Ahimelech had inquired of God for him.

questions.q: What were the servants of King Saul not willing to do?
questions.a: They were not willing to attack the priests of Yahweh.

questions.q: Whom did Doeg kill with the sword in Nob, the city of the priests?
questions.a: He killed men and women, children and infants, and oxen, donkeys, and sheep.

questions.q: Where did Abiathar go when he escaped the killing?
questions.a: Abiathar ran away and joined David.

questions.q: For what did David tell Abiathar he was responsible?
questions.a: David said that the death of every person in Abiathar’s father’s house was his fault.

commentary.text: David at Adullam, Many resort to him.
Saul destroys the priests of Nob.

Verses 1–5 See what weak instruments God sometimes uses, to bring about his own purposes. The Son of David is ready to receive distressed souls, who will be commanded by him. He receives all who come unto Him, however vile and miserable; he changes them into a holy people, and employs them in his service: those who would reign with him must be contented first to suffer with and for him. Observe with what tender concern David provided for his aged parents. The first thing he does is to find them a quiet habitation, whatever became of himself. Let children learn to honour their parents, in every thing consulting their ease and satisfaction. Though highly preferred, and much employed, let them not forget their aged parents. The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord. And the Lord will preserve his people for their appointed work, however they may be hated and exposed.

See the nature of jealous malice and its pitiful arts. Saul looks upon all about him as his enemies, because they do not just say as he says. In Ahimelech's answer to Saul we have the language of conscious innocence. But what wickedness will not the evil spirit hurry men to when he gets the dominion! Saul alleges that which was utterly false and unproved. But the most bloody tyrants have found instruments of their cruelty as barbarous as themselves. Doeg, having murdered the priests, went to the city, Nob, and put all to the sword there. Nothing so vile but those may do it, who have provoked God to give them up to their hearts' lusts. Yet this was the accomplishment of the threatenings against the house of Eli. Though Saul was unrighteous in doing this, yet God was righteous in permitting it. No word of God shall fall to the ground.

David greatly lamented the calamity. It is great trouble to a good man to find himself any way the cause of evil to others. He must have been much pained, when he considered that his falsehood was one cause of this fatal event. David speaks with assurance of his own safety, and promises that Abiathar should have his protection. With the Son of David, all who are his may be sure they shall be in safeguard, Ps 91:1. In the hurry and distraction David was continually in, he found time for communion with God, and found comfort in it.
